Wheels show up in Mesopotamia, first for pottery and then for carts.
Scribes in Sumerian cities like Uruk start writing on clay tablets, one of the world's first writing systems.
Upper and Lower Egypt are joined into one kingdom, traditionally by King Narmer.
The first stage of Stonehenge, a circular ditch and bank, is built in southern Britain.
The Great Pyramid is completed for the pharaoh Khufu. It stays the tallest building on Earth for nearly 4,000 years.
Planned cities like Mohenjo-daro have grid streets, drains and public baths.
Sargon of Akkad conquers the Sumerian cities, creating what is often called the first empire.
King Hammurabi of Babylon sets out 282 laws carved in stone.
Egypt's Thutmose III defeats a Canaanite coalition: the first battle recorded in detail.
Egypt's Ramesses II fights the Hittites in one of the largest chariot battles ever.
Shang dynasty diviners carve the earliest known Chinese writing on bones and shells.
The Olmecs, famous for giant stone heads, flourish around San Lorenzo in Mexico.
The first recorded Olympic Games are held at Olympia in Greece.
According to legend, Romulus founds the city of Rome.
King Piye of Kush, from today's Sudan, conquers Egypt and starts its 25th dynasty.
The Assyrians capture Samaria and end the northern Kingdom of Israel.
Babylonians and Medes destroy Nineveh, the Assyrian capital.
Nebuchadnezzar II takes Jerusalem and destroys the First Temple.
Confucius, whose teachings shape China for over 2,000 years, is born in the state of Lu.
The Persian king Cyrus the Great captures Babylon.
Cleisthenes' reforms give Athenian citizens a direct vote: an early democracy.
Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, teaches in northern India (his dates are uncertain).
Athens defeats a Persian invasion. The legend of the runner to Athens inspires the marathon.
A small Greek force led by 300 Spartans holds off the Persian army for three days.
The Greek fleet crushes the Persian navy, turning back Xerxes' invasion.
Work begins on the Parthenon, Athena's temple on the Acropolis.
Athens and Sparta begin a 27-year war for control of Greece.
The philosopher Socrates is tried and sentenced to death in Athens.
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III; the Persian Empire falls.
Alexander founds Alexandria in Egypt, later home of the great Library.
Alexander the Great dies in Babylon at 32, and his generals divide his empire.
After this bloody conquest, the Indian emperor Ashoka turns to Buddhism and nonviolence.
Qin Shi Huang conquers the last rival states and becomes China's first emperor.
Carthage's general Hannibal leads an army, with elephants, over the Alps into Italy.
Hannibal surrounds and destroys a much larger Roman army.
The first emperor links older walls into an early Great Wall of China.
Rome's Scipio defeats Hannibal, ending the Second Punic War.
Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty, which rules China for four centuries.
Rome destroys Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War.
A Han envoy's journey to Central Asia helps open the Silk Road.
Julius Caesar leads his army into Italy, starting a civil war.
Senators stab Julius Caesar to death in Rome on the Ides of March.
Octavian defeats Mark Antony and Cleopatra at sea.
Octavian takes the name Augustus and becomes Rome's first emperor.
Jesus of Nazareth is born in Judea, probably a few years before 1 CE.
Germanic tribes ambush and destroy three Roman legions.
Roman legions land in Britain and begin its conquest.
A fire burns for six days and destroys much of Rome.
Roman forces capture Jerusalem and destroy the Second Temple.
Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash.
Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD
Rome's great amphitheatre opens with 100 days of games.
Court official Cai Lun is credited with improving papermaking in Han China.
Romans begin a wall across northern Britain.
The Han dynasty ends and China splits into the Three Kingdoms.
Maya cities like Tikal rise in Central America, with pyramids, writing and astronomy.
Emperor Constantine makes Byzantium his new capital, Constantinople.
Gothic warriors defeat a Roman army and kill Emperor Valens.
Rome is sacked by a foreign army for the first time in 800 years.
Romans and Visigoths halt Attila the Hun at the Catalaunian Plains.
Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Odoacer deposes the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Justinian's great church is completed in Constantinople.
Plague spreads across the Mediterranean world and kills millions.
The Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, is born in Mecca.
Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina; year one of the Islamic calendar.
Indian mathematician Brahmagupta writes down rules for calculating with zero.
Arab armies defeat the Byzantines and take control of Syria.
Muslim forces cross from North Africa and conquer most of Iberia.
Charles Martel's Franks stop an Umayyad army in France.
The Abbasids defeat Tang China in Central Asia.
Caliph al-Mansur builds the round city of Baghdad, soon one of the world's largest cities.
A Viking raid on an English monastery marks the start of the Viking Age.
The pope crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.
The Diamond Sutra is printed in China with carved wooden blocks.
The Song dynasty unifies China, an age of paper money, printing and gunpowder.
Leif Erikson's Norse sailors camp in Newfoundland, 500 years before Columbus.
The Christian church splits into Catholic and Orthodox branches.
William of Normandy defeats King Harold and conquers England.
Traditionally dated to 1088, Europe's oldest university opens.
Cahokia, near today's St. Louis, is the largest city north of Mexico, with huge earthen mounds.
The Khmer begin Angkor Wat, still the world's largest religious monument.
Minamoto no Yoritomo becomes shogun; warriors rule Japan for centuries.
Temüjin unites the Mongol tribes and is proclaimed Genghis Khan.
The Delhi Sultanate is founded and rules much of northern India for 300 years.
England's barons force King John to accept limits on royal power.
Sundiata Keita defeats his rivals and founds the Mali Empire.
Mongol armies destroy Baghdad and end the Abbasid caliphate.
Egypt's Mamluks defeat the Mongols, stopping their advance west.
The Venetian Marco Polo begins his journey to Kublai Khan's China.
Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty, ruling China from Khanbaliq (Beijing).
The last Song forces fall to the Mongols; all China is under Yuan rule.
The stone city of Great Zimbabwe is at its height as a trading center.
Mali's ruler travels to Mecca with so much gold that he lowers its price in Cairo.
The Mexica (Aztecs) found their island capital, traditionally in 1325.
Plague arrives in Sicily and kills perhaps a third of Europe's people.
Zhu Yuanzhang drives out the Mongols and founds the Ming dynasty.
China's admiral Zheng He sails the first of seven great fleets to Asia and Africa.
English longbowmen defeat a larger French army.
Pachacuti begins turning Cusco into the Inca Empire, the largest in the Americas.
Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press in Mainz transforms Europe.
The Incas build Machu Picchu high in the Andes.
The Ottomans capture Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.
Bartolomeu Dias sails around Africa's southern tip.
Columbus lands in the Bahamas, beginning lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.
Spain conquers Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Iberia.
Vasco da Gama reaches India by sailing around Africa.
Martin Luther publishes his Ninety-five Theses in Wittenberg.
The Ottoman Empire defeats the Mamluks and takes Cairo.
Magellan's expedition leaves Spain; one ship returns three years later, the first to circle the globe.
Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies capture the Aztec capital.
Babur wins in northern India and founds the Mughal Empire.
Spanish conquistadors seize the Inca emperor at Cajamarca.
Copernicus's book argues that the Earth goes around the Sun.
A Christian alliance defeats the Ottoman fleet in a great galley battle.
England fights off Spain's huge invasion fleet.
Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasion of Korea begins the Imjin War.
Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the battle that unifies Japan under his family.
Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun, ruling from Edo (Tokyo) for 265 years.
English settlers found Jamestown in Virginia.
Galileo turns a telescope to the sky and sees Jupiter's moons.
A revolt in Prague starts one of Europe's most destructive wars.
English Pilgrims arrive at Plymouth in Massachusetts.
Shah Jahan begins the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Manchu armies take Beijing; the Qing dynasty will rule China until 1912.
Treaties end the Thirty Years' War and shape Europe's system of sovereign states.
The Dutch East India Company sets up a supply station at the Cape.
A fire destroys most of the old City of London.
A Polish-led army breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna.
Isaac Newton publishes his laws of motion and gravity.
England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain.
An earthquake, tsunami and fires destroy much of Lisbon.
The British East India Company's victory begins its rule in India.
James Watt patents his improved steam engine, powering the Industrial Revolution.
James Cook lands at Botany Bay on Australia's east coast.
Thirteen American colonies declare independence from Britain.
British ships found a penal colony at Sydney Cove.
Parisians storm the Bastille prison; the French Revolution begins.
Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise up, leading to Haiti's independence in 1804.
Edward Jenner shows that cowpox protects against smallpox.
Haiti becomes the first nation founded after a successful slave revolt.
The Lewis and Clark expedition sets out to cross North America to the Pacific.
Nelson's British fleet defeats France and Spain at sea.
Napoleon defeats Austria and Russia in his most famous victory.
Miguel Hidalgo's Cry of Dolores starts Mexico's war of independence.
Napoleon reaches Moscow but loses most of his army on the retreat.
Napoleon is finally defeated by Wellington and Blücher.
The largest eruption in recorded history causes a 'year without a summer'.
Shaka builds the Zulu kingdom into a major power in southern Africa.
Simón Bolívar's victory frees much of northern South America from Spain.
Prince Pedro declares Brazil independent from Portugal.
Steam trains begin carrying passengers on England's Stockton and Darlington Railway.
Britain goes to war with Qing China over the opium trade.
British representatives and Māori chiefs sign New Zealand's founding treaty.
Revolutions sweep across Europe, starting in Paris.
Gold is found at Sutter's Mill and 300,000 people rush to California.
Soldiers in Meerut revolt against British East India Company rule.
Charles Darwin publishes his theory of evolution by natural selection.
Confederate forces fire on Fort Sumter.
The Union's victory turns the tide of the American Civil War.
President Abraham Lincoln is shot days after the Civil War ends.
Japan's emperor regains power and the country rapidly modernizes.
The canal links the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
A golden spike completes the first railroad across the United States.
The German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles.
Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone.
Thomas Edison's lab demonstrates a long-lasting light bulb.
The explosion is heard nearly 5,000 km away.
European powers set rules for dividing Africa among themselves.
The Golden Law abolishes slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to do so.
The Lumière brothers show films to a paying audience in Paris.
Ethiopia defeats an Italian invasion and stays independent.
Guglielmo Marconi sends the first transatlantic radio signal.
The Wright brothers fly at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
Albert Einstein publishes special relativity while working in Bern.
Japan destroys Russia's fleet, the first modern defeat of a European power by an Asian one.
An earthquake and fires destroy much of San Francisco.
An uprising in Wuchang ends 2,000 years of imperial rule in China.
Roald Amundsen's team is first to reach the South Pole.
The 'unsinkable' liner hits an iceberg on its first voyage.
The assassination in Sarajevo sets off World War I.
Ships can cross between the Atlantic and Pacific.
One of the longest and deadliest battles of World War I.
Over a million soldiers are killed or wounded.
The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd.
An armistice signed in a railway car ends the fighting.
The peace treaty with Germany is signed.
Howard Carter finds the boy pharaoh's tomb nearly untouched.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founds the Turkish Republic.
Alexander Fleming discovers the first antibiotic.
The stock market collapses, starting the Great Depression.
Gandhi walks to the sea to make salt, defying British law.
The Royal Air Force defends Britain against the German air force.
Japan attacks the US fleet in Hawaii, bringing the US into the war.
Nazi Germany murders six million Jews and millions of others; Auschwitz becomes its largest death camp.
The Soviet victory is a turning point of World War II.
The US drops atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Japan surrenders.
Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Fifty countries sign the UN Charter in San Francisco.
United Nations Conference on International Organization
British India is partitioned into two independent countries.
The State of Israel declares independence.
Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic in Beijing.
Proclamation of the People's Republic of China
Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reach the top of the world.
Scientists in Cambridge describe the structure of DNA.
The USSR launches the first artificial satellite.
Ghana becomes one of the first African colonies to win independence.
Fidel Castro's rebels take power in Cuba.
Nigeria and sixteen other African countries become independent.
East Germany seals off West Berlin with a wall.
The US and USSR come close to nuclear war over missiles in Cuba.
Martin Luther King Jr. speaks at the March on Washington.
Mao launches a decade of political upheaval in China.
Apollo 11, launched from Florida, lands the first people on the Moon.
North Vietnamese forces take Saigon, ending the Vietnam War.
Deng Xiaoping begins reforms that open China's economy.
A nuclear reactor explodes in Soviet Ukraine.
East Germans cross the Wall freely; the Cold War is ending.
Tim Berners-Lee proposes the Web at CERN.
The USSR breaks into 15 independent countries.
South Africa's first all-race election makes Nelson Mandela president.
About 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, are killed in 100 days.
Britain returns Hong Kong to China.
Transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong
Terrorist attacks in the United States kill nearly 3,000 people.
An earthquake off Sumatra sends tsunamis across the Indian Ocean.
A banking crisis spreads from the US to the world economy.
A huge earthquake and tsunami strike Japan, causing the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
A new coronavirus, first identified in Wuhan in late 2019, spreads worldwide.
